A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Thinking with Video and VideoThinkBench, with directly matchable tasks, experiments, and analyses. The complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Sora-2 benchmark results, few-shot and self-consistency experiments, reasoning-process analyses, and a Wan2.5 prompt-rewriting ablation.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical studies and adds comparisons involving additional video generators, image generators, and vision-language models in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The proposed video-generation reasoning approach, inputs and outputs, and existing few-shot and self-consistency procedures remain unchanged. Additional evaluated models are comparators; no new architecture, training objective, or proposed algorithmic component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same eyeballing puzzles, visual puzzles, ARC-AGI-2, three maze geometries, and text-centric benchmarks. V2's 750-sample mini set draws from the existing 4,149-sample benchmark. Renamed task groupings and additional model evaluations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Tables 7–8 substantially expand comparisons with Veo 3.1, MiniMax Hailuo 2.3, Seedance 1.0 Pro, MOVA, Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, five image generators, and Qwen3-VL variants. Image comparators include Nano Banana Pro, Seedream 4.5, GPT Image 1.5, BAGEL, and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511. V2 also adds Grok 4 to the ARC-AGI-2 comparison and VLM comparisons on mazes.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a separate 750-sample evaluation subset comprising 500 vision-centric and 250 text-centric samples. Table 1 switches text-centric summaries from last-frame to audio accuracy, and visual-puzzle aggregation changes from color/shape groups to symmetry/gradient/compositionality. Joint video/audio correctness metrics are dropped. The stated Perpendicular VLM prompt is corrected; unchanged scores do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds qualitative multimodal-question cases from MathVista, MMMU, and MMBench. Visual-puzzle subgroup analysis shifts from output type to reasoning type. The principal few-shot, self-consistency, numerical-perturbation, prompt-rewriting, and reasoning-error analyses remain substantially unchanged.

E5.justification: The stated Avg@4 AIME reporting and five-attempt self-consistency voting are retained. V2 adds no seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests; its new comparison tables continue reporting point accuracies.

E6.justification: Tables 7–8 add extensive mini-set results, including vision-centric averages of 31.6% for Sora-2, 27.7% for Veo 3.1, and 29.8% for Nano Banana Pro. All 13 retained text-benchmark rows are unchanged, but reported overall last-frame/audio averages change from 56.3/73.6 to 57.0/67.8. V2 also corrects the ARC summary to match v1 Table 4, reports new subgroup aggregates, and removes joint-modality result entries. These changes do not establish same-setting Sora-2 performance gains.

T1.justification: The visual-puzzle deviation definitions and equations remain equivalent, including RGB distance and binarized shape mismatch. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs; the new reasoning hierarchy is conceptual rather than mathematical.

C1.justification: Some headline performance claims now use audio scores already reported in v1: abstract MMMU accuracy changes from 75.53% to 69.2%, and introductory MATH accuracy from 94% to 92%. The eyeballing advantage is specified against GPT-5. The central paradigm, benchmark, few-shot learning, and self-consistency contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 introduces a five-ability hierarchy and a rationale connecting visual text learning with language reasoning. Its visual-puzzle interpretation emphasizes competitiveness with Claude on symmetry rather than shape-drawing tasks. The strong characterization of temporal consistency as a confidence proxy is removed, while the prompt-rewriter hypothesis and closed-model limitation remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the mini-set composition and changes the benchmark access link from the fnlp namespace to OpenMOSS-Team. Conversely, it omits the exact ARC-AGI-2 prompt and detailed palette-based grid extraction procedure, and removes the official-result markers for AIME25 and GPQA comparators. Most other prompts and generation parameters are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for new comparators and visual text learning, including DeepSeek-OCR and See the Text. Section 4 now explicitly acknowledges quantitative evaluations in earlier video-reasoning work and presents this benchmark as complementary, while adding a first-systematic-comparison claim concerning Thinking with Images. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The main evaluation and analysis sections are extensively condensed and rewritten around reasoning capabilities. Detailed protocols and results move into reorganized appendices, and prompts are consolidated into Appendix F. Terminology, affiliations, and correspondence information are also revised.

P2.justification: V2 adds bar-chart presentations of retained eyeballing and visual-puzzle results while moving their detailed tables to the appendix. Numerous overview and case figures are redrawn or rearranged; new mini-set tables and multimodal examples are added. Reasoning examples move into the main text, the category-distribution chart moves to the appendix, and joint-modality table columns disappear.

improvement.justification: V1's broad paradigm claims relied chiefly on Sora-2 versus three VLMs. V2 Tables 7–8 add comparisons with other video generators and direct image-generation alternatives on a common mini set, substantially strengthening assessment of where video reasoning is competitive. Corrected summary inconsistencies and clearer organization also help. Removed joint-modality statistics and ARC implementation details reduce transparency, but the expanded comparative evidence addresses a substantial weakness and supports a clear overall improvement.
